channel.title: HTTP on Humus
channel.description: Recent content in HTTP on Humus

item.title: Serving HTTP
item.description: The httpserver package serves an http.Handler over TLS as a humus.Service. The end user’s Init sources its Settings, builds the Service with httpserver.NewService and returns it, and httpserver.Main runs it with the defaults an HTTP server behind a load balancer needs: a 5s drain and a 10s grace period. Its test package, httpservertest, runs the same App in a test, on the same defaults, with an HTTP/2 client. Serving HTTP/3 serves the same handler over HTTP/3 beside it.

item.title: Serving HTTP/3
item.description:
The http3server package serves an http.Handler over HTTP/3 as a humus.Service. It is in the nested module github.com/z5labs/humus/http3, which keeps quic-go out of the core module. No quic-go type is in its API, and none of httpserver’s: it has its own Settings, DefaultSettings, a check per field, Defaults and Main. Its test package, http3servertest, runs the same App in a test, on the same defaults, with an HTTP/3 client.

HTTP/3 is served beside Serving HTTP’s Service, not in place of it, so it is off unless the end user’s Init returns it. The design is in Proposal: HTTP/3, with its revision 1 and revision 2.

item.title: Serving an API with OpenAPI
item.description:
The openapi/v3 package serves an API of typed operations, and its OpenAPI document. The end user’s Init declares each operation once, on a typed path, with a typed handler and the codecs of its bodies, builds the API with openapi.NewAPI, and hands it to httpserver.NewService, which serves it over TLS as Serving HTTP describes. The same declarations serve the requests and write the document, so the two can’t disagree.

The import path names the major version of OpenAPI the package follows, and the package’s name is openapi. Two packages beside it are opt-in, and openapi uses neither: jsoncodec reads and writes JSON bodies, and problem answers errors with RFC 9457 problem details. The design behind everything on this page is in Proposal: OpenAPI endpoint DSL, as its revisions 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 amend it.

item.title: Serving a hypermedia UI
item.description:
The hypermedia package serves the pages, fragments and actions of a hypermedia-driven UI, as the http.Handler that httpserver serves. The sse package writes its event streams. Neither knows a client library: the headers, attributes, events and status codes a library reads are the end user’s, and Your library decides shows them.

The code on this page is example/http/inlineedit, a list of contacts edited in place, with a live feed of every saved row. It serves the same UI twice: htmxui with htmx, and datastarui with Datastar. Both share the contacts package: the paths, the form’s fields, the store, the error page and the assets.
